stillWaitingOnIt: Nothing. No row in backlog.json or any themes/*/backlog.json lists inc-245 or obligation-model in dependsOn, and the row's own notes say nothing waits for it. report.md:925 claims every feature theme's markings rest on it, but the feature rows have shipped page-level hard stops without it: inc-232 and inc-240 are done, EUDPA-760 is merged. Rows that overlap it: inc-232 (done, both save buttons make the same checks and documents are all-or-nothing on every button), inc-231 (dropped into inc-232), inc-240 (done, transporter hard stop), inc-243 (consignment-parties, todo) and inc-244 (germinal-products, todo, which covers germinal quantity, the one germinal field V4 marks mandatory to proceed). recommendation:
Drop it. The behaviour it promises is already on main, built a different way.

Hard stops are each page's own validation, added page by page in the feature themes. Submission checks are the obligation status plus the review page's refusal. Both save buttons now make the same checks (inc-232). The one all-or-nothing group in V4, accompanying documents, is refused when half-filled on every button and reads complete when empty or full. The model has also had allOrNothingOfIds since September.

Each remaining mandatory-to-proceed field belongs on its own page's row. inc-243 covers the parties pages and inc-244 the germinal pages; origin and transporters are already done.

What is lost if dropped: the model would never record 'mandatory to proceed' as its own marking. Whether a field is a hard stop would stay in page code, not in the manifest. No single test suite (the obligation-markings E2E) would prove the four markings together. Nothing in the release needs these things.

If Sam wants that single source of truth later, it is a refactor and can be raised as one.

corrections: Small fix, verdict unchanged. The recommendation says only origin and transporters are 'already done', which undercounts. On main, other pages already refuse a blank required answer before you can leave them: reason for import (import-reason/validate.js uses requiredOneOf for purpose, destination country and port of exit), contact (contact/validate.js, contactRequired) and port of entry (means of transport). The isHubExit/allowMissing bypass is gone. Every field in the documents collection is mandatory, with no minEntries and maxEntries 15. startsADocument and refuseUnaddedDocument are at controller.js:402-403. The tests repo has no obligation-markings folder. The row has dependsOn [], and nothing else in the backlog references inc-245. The documents block is the only all-or-nothing group in V4, and germinal Quantity is the one germinal field marked mandatory to proceed (p5-074).
verdict.finalRecommendation:
Drop the obligation-model row (the one about telling a hard stop from a submission check and keeping groups all-or-nothing). What it promises is already on main, built a different way.

- Hard stops: each page's own validation does this. Origin, reason for import, contact, port of entry and transporters already refuse a blank required answer.
- Submission checks: the obligation status and the review page's refusal handle these.
- Both save buttons: they make the same checks since the design-snagging fix.
- Accompanying documents: the one all-or-nothing group in V4. It is refused when half-filled and reads complete when empty or full.
- 'At least one' (animal identifiers): already in the model as anyOfIds.
- Conditional answers: already judged per scope by applyTo.

The mandatory-to-proceed fields still open belong to their own rows:
- consignment parties: inc-243
- germinal quantity: inc-244
- commodity, type, species and number of animals: the separate commodities search ticket

What is lost: the manifest would never name 'mandatory to proceed' as its own marking, and no single E2E suite would prove all the markings together. Nothing in the release needs either. If Sam later wants the manifest to be the single source of truth, raise that as a refactor.

The open question about how far the save-button checks reach (c-372) is about each page's checks, not the model, so dropping this row loses nothing there.

verdict.finalRecommendation:
Keep the row (live animals browser tests that prove looks by class list), but trim it as the colleague says.

**Drop:**
- The Overview screenshot and the transit-countries screenshot: both are already on tests main.
- The stale reason for keeping transporters here: the transporters theme has 11 done and 2 blocked.

**Build now:** the parts no other theme will touch.
- Arrival details labels, hint colour and transit remove column (arrival-transit.fit).
- Upload documents actions column (upload.fit).
- Size classes on origin, consignment details, additional details and import reason.
- The section caption.
- Transporter tags, bold text and legends.
- The type-ahead work: an accented-search browser test (today unit tests only), label size read at run time, one owner for the '.app-autocomplete__button' selector, a shared computed-style reader, and moving expectStyle or fixing the testing guide at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/docs/testing.md:81.
- Screenshots for arrival details, Upload documents and the review's last card. None exist yet.

**Hub and review parts:** only move them into overview-and-review if the clean-up is written into those rows.
- What to add: inc-098 for the hub totals box, buttons and caption line height; inc-101 or inc-117 for the review's visually-hidden and summary-card class checks.
- Otherwise they lose their only owner: inc-101, inc-110 and inc-117 don't mention them today.
- The cost of moving: they then wait behind identification-and-permanent-address, which hasn't been split yet (10 todo rows).
- The alternative: keep them here and do them after overview-and-review lands.

**Don't drop the whole row.** That would lose the only plan to bring these tests into line with the programme rule, and the only planned browser test of accented type-ahead search.

So drop the commodity acceptance criterion and the 27 Oct notes for commodity-question-detour.js and kit.js.

What is left, all in animals-frontend:
- Switch partyEditHref (edit-href.js:10) to kit.withReturnMarker, keeping its call signature.
- Switch the hard-coded 'cph-number?return=addresses' link (addresses/controller.js:57) to the shared builder. The row does not name this one yet.
- Move HTML_ESCAPES and MATCH_CLASS inside the functions that use them, matching the plants copy of bold-matches.js, which already does this.
- Delete src/client/common/helpers/.gitkeep.

If the row is dropped, nothing changes for users. The code keeps two hand-built return links beside the shared builder, a small breach of the house rule on literals, and a dead file. None of it is test work, so it also suits merging into a general code-tidy row if one exists. Nothing depends on it.

recommendation: Keep it as it is. All five criteria still hold on main, checked item by item, and nothing has fixed any of them since 27 October. It is small, low-risk test and doc work in plants-frontend, ins-tests and the workspace openspec, and it can be built now: arrival-and-transit has merged and left plants arrival-details untouched. If it were dropped, the plants guide would keep a false coverage claim and a broken sentence, and the plants arrival labels would stay the last class-list checks against the house rule. The landing and genus accent matching would also stay out of the behaviour spec, and plants screenshots would have no command of their own. corrections: Two of the files the row touches have changed since 27 October. On 6 Nov, d66241e (EUDPA-690, the 'What are you importing?' type question) rewrote the plants testing guide's picker paragraph and 44 lines of fit/high-risk-plants-journey.js. The coverage claim is false, as the colleague says. Shared helpers live in fit/, outside src/, so neither vitest (which covers src/**/*.js) nor sonar (whose sources are src/ minus *.fit.spec.js) would count them. Builders should fix the wording, not move code.

The README's plants row is correct to show dashes for a11y and security: tests/plants/a11y and tests/plants/security hold only a .gitkeep. Only the visual dash is wrong, because tests/plants/e2e/visual has four specs with baselines. The fix is the visual cell plus a test:docker-compose:plants:visual script. Nothing more is needed.

Sam's 10 Nov ruling that commodity search is handled by a separate ticket covers the animals commodity search row inc-014 (the joined search button, search as you type, germinal codes). It does not cover the plants genus type-ahead on Commodity details, which is already built and tested ('Cást'). So the genus accent wording in this row is not blocked by that ruling.
verdict.finalRecommendation:
Keep it as it is. I re-checked every criterion on origin/main and all five still hold:

- The plants testing guide has a false coverage claim and a broken sentence.
- The fit readers in high-risk-plants-journey.js, type-ahead.fit.spec.js and arrival-details.fit.spec.js rename their arguments on the way into the page.
- The only plants class-list checks left are toHaveClass(/govuk-label--m/) on arrival-details (lines 182 and 298).
- The plants behaviour spec does not say the landing and genus searches ignore case and accents. The origin spec already says this for countries.
- The tests repo has no plants screenshot command, and the README's plants visual cell shows a dash.

The 6 Nov commit d66241e changed the guide and the journey helper without fixing any of this.

The arrival-and-transit theme has merged and did not touch plants arrival-details, so nothing blocks the build. Sam's commodity search ruling is about the animals search, not the plants genus type-ahead.

Dropping the row would lose small but real fixes: wrong text in the guide, the last label checks that test a CSS class against the house rule, a gap in the spec where the tests already prove accent matching, and the missing command.

For whoever builds it:
- Reword the coverage claim (fit/ sits outside src/ anyway); don't move code.
- Fix only the README's plants visual cell. The a11y and security dashes are right, because those folders are empty.
